title: Lamb Tagine with Apricots and Almonds
subtitle: Moroccan slow-braised lamb with sweet and savoury spices
excerpt: A Moroccan classic: chunks of lamb shoulder slow-braised in a fragrant spice broth with dried apricots, honey, and almonds until the meat is falling tender and the sauce is thick and glossy. Warm spicing with a gentle, fruit-forward sweetness.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tagine refers both to the distinctive conical earthenware vessel in which these Moroccan braises are cooked and to the braise itself. The cone-shaped lid circulates steam back onto the food, creating a self-basting environment that requires very little liquid. The combination of meat with dried fruit and nuts is a defining characteristic of Moroccan cooking, reflecting the country's position at the crossroads of Andalusian Arab, Berber, and sub-Saharan African culinary traditions. The spice blend known as ras el hanout (head of the shop, meaning the best spices) varies by vendor and household; the key notes are warm spices: cinnamon, cumin, ginger, coriander, and saffron. The version here uses accessible spices to approximate this blend without requiring a specialist spice mix.

content.text: If you do not have a tagine, a heavy casserole with a lid works perfectly. Brown the lamb well before braising: this step is often skipped in tagines but gives the sauce much more depth. The braise uses very little liquid; resist the urge to add water unless the pot is completely dry.

content.text: Heat the oven to 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3. Season the lamb with salt. Heat the oil in a heavy flameproof casserole and brown the lamb all over in batches. Remove and set aside. Cook the onion in the remaining fat for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and all the ground spices. Stir for 1 minute.
Return the lamb. Add the tomatoes, stock, saffron water, and honey. Bring to a simmer. Cover tightly and cook in the oven for 1 hour 15 minutes.

Add the dried apricots. Cover and cook for a further 30 minutes until the lamb is very tender and the sauce is thick. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve over couscous, topped with toasted almonds and fresh coriander.
